newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower on moderate volumes.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower on moderate volumes.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended lower Monday, in line with LME copper, as the market corrected from the six-month highs seen in late November on expectations of more builds in LME warehouse copper stocks Tuesday.
COMEX March copper ended down 1.45 cents at 98.60 cents, after trading in a 100.10-98.25 cent range, inside Friday's wide range.

"Copper futures remain very sensitive to the bi-weekly LME stock updates and the cash-to-three month LME backwardation as indicators of the degree of supply tightness in the cash market," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.

LME warehouse copper stocks, which saw a six year low in last month, have risen in the past week, posting a 6,400 tonne gain Friday to 99,875 tonnes and are expected to see another 3,000-5,000 tonne rise Tuesday.
Traders said the rise in LME stocks in recent weeks was due to metal from COMEX going into the London exchange's depot after the arbitrage between COMEX and LME switched in favor of LME.
Meanwhile, COMEX copper stocks fell 1,981 short tons Monday to 24,033 short tons.
The December/March backwardation slipped to 4.60 cents Monday after briefly narrowing to 3.50 cents last week, from a high of 5.50 cents on December 2.
COMEX March copper saw a six month high at 105.05 cents on November 27, driven by a tight prompt market, but has since been consolidating, with supplies seen rising in 1997.

But year-to-date refined copper demand is up about 2.2 pct for the year, Smith Barney analyst Victor Lazarovici said, while new supply is coming on more slowly than expected with copper prices below $1.00 a deterrent to smelter expansion.
Total refined inventories look to have fallen to about 3.7 weeks on consumption, well below the industry norm of around five weeks, he said.

Meanwhile, total speculative (funds plus small traders) net long open interest in COMEX copper futures remains around 21,585 lots, according to the CFTC Commitment of Traders data for the week ended December 3, issued late Friday.
"With copper stocks at critically low levels, unexpected supply or demand shocks could trigger a significant price response," Smith Barney's Rinehimer said.
